newsitem.title: USA: Price Waterhouse to consolidate in NYC - Pataki.
newsitem.headline: Price Waterhouse to consolidate in NYC - Pataki.

text.p: New York Gov. George Pataki said Thursday accounting firm Price Waterhouse LLT agreed to consolidate in New York City, creating 1,090 jobs in addition to its current workforce of 2,200.

Pataki declined to say who the state had competed with to keep the accounting giant, saying only, "I can tell you there was no guarantee on this. Officials of Price Waterhouse were looking throughout the tri-state region."

Noting McGraw Hill recently decided to keep more than 4,000 jobs in the city, the governor, who held a news conference in New York City, said his administration and New York City Mayor Rudolph Giuliani were winning the battle to retain big employers.
"It has been a really remarkable turnaround," he said, saying Giuliani's efforts to make the city safer and cleaner were paying off.

The accounting firm, which has had a New York City office since 1890, expects to add 1,090 accountants, consultants, management advisory and computer staffers, whose salaries will range from entry-level to six figures, over the next three to five years, said Brett Yacker, a partner. Price Waterhouse, which is headquartered at 1177 Sixth Avenue, plans to expand into 140,000 square feet of space at 11 Madison Avenue.

To keep Price Waterhouse, Empire State Development Corp agreed to provide a $1.5 million job creation grant, a $500,000 capital improvement for the new offices, and state and city sales tax exemptions, linked to its expansion, over ten years.

Price Waterhouse has 56,000 employees in 119 countries. Its New York State offices are on Long Island and in Rochester, Buffalo and Syracuse. Including the new jobs, the firm's total state payroll will be over $225 million a year. million, according the governor's prepared statement.
